summary: The household's pool of tools, weapons and consumables (scripts/companion/tool_pool.gd; user 2026-09-29: 'for the supply chain we need to add a household pool of tools and items they can use and bring back'). Everything the household owns that its workers borrow lives in the real containers: tools and consumables in the storage chests (counted through the store, as the food is), long weapons in the musket racks and spear barrels (PlacedWeapon nodes, with their state). A worker's job names the tools it needs (data/companion/jobs.json `tools`, joined with what the survival rules ask of its action: actions.json requires.tools and its recipes' tools); the job is not planned when none is free; she claims them when it is planned, walks to the chest or rack for them, carries them (in her right hand where there is a model) through a run of that job and the next of the same, and puts them back when she changes job and at the end of her day. Tools wear with every run they were used in and break when their durability is used up (or, rarely, before); broken ones are shown in the Tasks tab until a new one is put in a chest. A worker who leaves or dies returns what she held.
kinds_note: Pool kinds are chest or rack kinds of their own (never the player's loadout kinds: the chest screen would lose a felling axe or a knife the player must always have): 'axe' is the household's felling axe, 'trade_knife' its skinning knife, 'flint_steel' its fire kit. Aliases (below) let the other work name the player's kinds. store: 'chest' (a storage chest keeps it: the player hands over spares through the ordinary chest screen) or 'rack' (a WeaponRack slot holds it as a PlacedWeapon of rack_key, with the weapon's state; E on a rack puts a carried weapon in as ever; rack_style: the kind of rack it prefers). item: the survival core item the rules look for while a worker carries it ("" none: a tool the rules do not know). durability: runs of work before it is worn out (wear_per_run, default 1, each run of a job that used it); break_chance: the odds a run breaks it outright. model: what she holds in her right hand ([library, kind]: gather = GatherModels, wildlife = WildlifeModels, throwable = ThrowableModels; [] shows nothing), grip: metres up the model's own +Y from its origin to where the fist closes; state: what a rack weapon is put back with when it has no state of its own.
jobs_note: A job's tools (data/companion/jobs.json `tools`, ToolPool.needs_of): need: [[kind, ...], ...] any-of groups, every group required (the first free kind of a group is taken; what she holds already serves first); optional: [[kind, ...]] or [{any: [kind, ...], speed: minutes factor}] taken when free (a timed job's minutes times speed); use: {kind: units} consumables a run takes (what is left comes back). Joined with what the survival rules ask of the job's action (actions.json requires.tools -> need, tools_optional -> optional) and its variants' recipes (recipes.json tools), mapped from the rules' items to the kinds below by `item`.
api_note: ToolPool (scripts/companion/tool_pool.gd): checkout(worker, needs) -> {ok, items, reason}; return_all(worker); available(kind, owner); held_by(worker); counts(); HuntKit's source shape count(kind, owner) / take(kind, n, owner) / put_back(kind, n, owner) and spend(worker, kind, n) for a consumable used.

climb_stakes.name: Climbing stakes
climb_stakes.note: a pair of climbing stakes: the workers carry them on the jobs outside, and with them get over what is chest high (1.5 m, a mantle) where without them a mini-vault takes 1.0 m (Spouse.abilities, WalkGrid.PERSON)

consumables_note: Counted store kinds a job or a trip uses up (jobs.json tools.use; the hunt's powder and ball): item and qty say what one unit is in her core (qty of the item). What she does not use comes back to the store; a part unit is kept by the pool until it makes a whole one.
worker_kit_note: A new worker's own belongings: only what she wears (these item categories) and the personal items listed here (e.g. "item.tool.knife" for a belt knife of her own); the survival background's kit is not hers. A worker from before the pool (an old save) and a recruit bring their kit's tools, weapons and consumables into the pool when they join (recruits_bring, legacy_bring), once; the wife and the workers born or made in the household start with nothing of the background's.
start_note: A new game's pool, put in the fort's chests and racks once the fort is furnished (FortPlan): chest kinds by count, rack kinds by pieces (each a rack weapon with its state). farm: the fields' tools (FARM: the hoe job), put in the chests once on their own, so an older save gets them too.
break_note: wear_per_run of a tool that was used in a run; a tool at its durability is broken (kept in the pool's broken list, not in a chest).
